questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
The host country should be far away, so that I could experience new cultures. The host nation should also have lots of nature and activities to do. Furthermore, there should be opportunities to travel the country and explore more than only the host city.
For me personally, it should also have been a developed country, due to safety concerns.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Housing was very difficult to find, and not much information/help was given. Furthermore, housing was very expensive in my opinion.
Also, I rarely got any information about study start and all the activities that were happening at the university and the city, even though I regularly checked my email and other official channels.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I had to do a lot of digging on the different platforms, in order to find the information needed. Would have been nice with a calendar prepared with links and other important deadlines.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not receive any. I knew people who lived at the host country, however, all information and practical things I had to go find and ask on my own. I got no tutor or mentor I could ask questions. It was only when I made friends with my peers that I found out when stuff was happening. Sometimes on the day when events were being held.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Very difficult. Either the housing was very sketchy or far away from campus. Otherwise it was only available for females, Indians or 1+ year lease terms. 
Furthermore, It was very expensive, and sometimes when I asked around the landlord did things off the record (no contract and all cash), making it very difficult to find a place before arriving.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Start searching almost 6 months in advance, and if possible, live in the "westdale" area. This is where most students live. Also don't worry about transportation cost. Public transport in Hamilton is free for McMaster students. You just need to buy the presto card.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I lived in a bad place, with nice people. Area and view were great as it was at lake Ontario, however the apartment were a health danger in my opinion, which I did not know before hand. There were cockroaches and mice, because the people I lived with did not know how to clean.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: super easy, but difficult to find information

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Super easy, everything is online.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could always email the department and ask for help in registration for a course. not sure this would be the same case for undergrad students, as I was in grad school

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got into all the classes I wanted, and even had the opportunity to change class within the first week as I found one of the classes I took, not to be to my liking.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: More information about which Courses is being offered at different terms. I could not find this information. Therefore, a few of the courses I wanted to take was not being offered at the time, even though they were on the official course website.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: more information about course and course content would have been nice. I found most of my courses to be boring as it was mostly paper reviews.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
Some of the courses covered very basic introductory level stuff, and not really advance stuff in my opinion. The level of homework was also very easy as it was mostly describe a graph or plot a graph. 
Furthermore, one course was purely paper reviews.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I liked it as it forced me to participate more in the class. (there were presentation and participation scores)

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
CAS 739, Evolutionary computation
CAS 764, Advance topics in data management
CAS 775, Theoretical Foundations of Unsupervised Learning

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Evolutionary computation is a fun course, as it is very different from traditional machine learning.
CAS 764 is fun as a reading course.
CAS 775 is a lot of math.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Food and cellphone planes cost to be so high. Also tipping is a huge thing in Canada, so be prepared to tip between 18%-20% every time you eat out.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Groceries were expensive. 
Eating out was surprisingly cheap (relatively)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Its an ivy league university. So they have everything. Nature, spots facilities (all sports), pools and a gym on campus.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You could attend and use any of the sports facilities as you wish. The pool were more restricted, however the outdoor club is great with lots of hikes and camping trips.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Hikes! there are over 100 waterfalls in Hamilton, and lots of great nature

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go to Niagara falls, or Toronto! it only cost 10$ for transportation for a full day on the weekends.
rent a car, see the national parks.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: People are friendly! there are also lots of social activities where you can meet other people and get new friends!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to the mix clubs, social gatherings! don't be afraid to ask other exchange students! many are in the same situration like yourself!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Drinking. What we perceive as normal in Europe or Denmark is very different from north America.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openess of people

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be open and don't be afraid to explore! don't sit at home all the time, you can do this in Dk.
Make some new friends, be open to what they like to do, and don't be afraid to go on your own to explore new places. But be prepared to use a lot of money!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
be careful when going to clubs, and around dodgy areas. People are not the same as here in Dk, and can be more aggressive and easily offended. 
Also make sure to carry some cash around! not everywhere uses credit or debit cards like in dk.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making new friends and growing as a person.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Making new friends.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
